note: Initial hypotheses for the first diagnostic round; no prior HYPOTHESES.json survived #256. Statuses are updated only from measured evidence in DIAGNOSIS.md and the probe JSON.

hypotheses.statement: R05's three-level codebooks reproduce the encoder output almost exactly (quantisation error 0.0071, effective rank 4.33), so hard assignments are near item-unique and structural/curvature changes have little shared-prefix slack.

The learned topology gates collapse toward one curvature expert (final gate entropy 0.58, level-3 mean weight 0.95 on one expert), and the topology tokens add little separable structure beyond degree, so the gate does not transmit local topology into the hard cost.

The frozen eight-role graphlet table is too coarse or too imbalanced for per-item geometry: roles 2 and 1 cover 65.7% of items, and the learned role mixtures may be near-uniform or dominated by one expert, so moving the role-conditioned mixture between levels cannot change hard L2 prefixes.

Null: the R05 test Recall@10 difference from the frozen baseline is ordinary Stage3 optimisation variance; no R05 SID property causally changes recommendation, so another mechanism must first improve an independently measured SID property.

The behaviour signal is concentrated at L1: R05's positive prefix hit rate falls from 0.060 at L1 to 0.0043 at L2 and 0.00047 at L3 (negative rates 0.0084 / 0.00025 / 6e-6), so deeper refinement is nearly behaviour-random and the L2/L3 partition is the recommendation bottleneck.

The assignment rule leaves the refinement unconstrained: only the last level uses Sinkhorn, earlier levels take floor-constrained nearest assignment, and 3 x 256 codes over 24,587 items yield 9,609 L2 prefixes with 2.56 items per prefix; capacity is spent on identity rather than shared structure.

Because cost-only switches move at most 1.7% of hard codes, the next legal lever is to let the frozen graphlet role partition the L2 candidate set inside the existing curvature cost; role then changes assignment, not just weights.

Adding the masked GNN token mean, projected by an identity-initialized linear map, to the level-2 assignment target changes the hard L2/L3 codes enough to coarsen L2 prefixes and increase behavior-pair prefix hits without changing L1.

The topology token offset must be expressed at the level-2 codebook resolution; the raw identity offset has norm 2.42 against a mean L2 codeword norm 0.046 and collapses the codebook before epoch 1400.
